title: AI-Augmented Variant Interpretation in Ovarian Cancer
text:
Lesson 2 — RNA fusion analysis
Gene fusions can be therapeutically relevant.
Examples in the source lesson include:

BCR-ABL
EML4-ALK

Fusion calling remains technically challenging because of:

unknown fusion partners
low gene expression
cryptic splice sites
difficult breakpoint mapping
poor-quality or low-cellularity specimens

title: AI-Augmented Variant Interpretation in Ovarian Cancer
text:
RNAfusion
RNAfusion is presented in the source lesson as an nf-core pipeline for RNA-seq fusion analysis.
Key characteristics:

standardized workflow
reproducible
portable
Nextflow-based
Docker / Singularity containerization
HPC and cloud integration
HTML reports
nf-core validation / linting

title: AI-Augmented Variant Interpretation in Ovarian Cancer
text:
RNAfusion — execution concept
Example from the source lesson:
nextflow run nf-core/rnafusion -profile test,docker
Why this matters clinically
Reproducibility is not only convenience.
It supports:

traceable software environments
consistent workflow execution
easier validation and re-analysis

title: AI-Augmented Variant Interpretation in Ovarian Cancer
text:
RNAfusion — fusion evidence
The source lesson also mentions kallisto fusion support:

reads spanning potential fusion breakpoints
--fusion mode
output to fusion.txt
downstream processing by pizzly

Masterclass question
What level of analytical evidence is required before a fusion enters clinical interpretation?

Fusion AI prompt — unsafe

An RNA fusion was detected between gene A and gene B.
Is it actionable and what therapy should be given?

Why unsafe?

breakpoint evidence
reading frame
transcript context
quality metrics
tumor type
evidence tier
regulatory context

title: AI-Augmented Variant Interpretation in Ovarian Cancer
text:
Fusion AI prompt — constrained
Use only the following evidence:

ANALYTICAL
- split-read count
- spanning-pair count
- breakpoint coordinates
- mapping quality
- strand orientation
- in-frame / out-of-frame status

CLINICAL
- tumor type
- AMP/ASCO/CAP tier
- ESCAT level if available

Return:
1. analytical evidence
2. biological interpretation
3. actionability requiring external verification
4. unsupported conclusions

title: AI-Augmented Variant Interpretation in Ovarian Cancer

B — supported biological inference
C — requires external evidence
D — unsupported / hallucinated
